entries.falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buyers keep committing to more accelerators than NVIDIA can build, so the company sells everything it makes and still carries a large unfilled order book.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a cut in cloud capital-spending plans, which would shrink the forward order book before shipments ever slow.
entries.statement: Datacenter GPU demand continues to outrun NVIDIA's ability to serve it.
entries.title: NVDA demand durability

entries.falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
entries.mechanism: Every accelerator needs both a stack of high-speed memory and a slot on an advanced packaging line, so whichever of the two is scarcer sets the shipment ceiling.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new packaging lines and memory fabs come online relative to each new accelerator generation's memory content.
entries.statement: Memory and advanced packaging are both capping how much merchant-GPU vendors can ship, with high-bandwidth memory sold out through 2027 and TSMC packaging booked out at 52 to 78 week lead times even as capacity climbs toward 130,000 wafers a month.
entries.title: Supply constraint binding

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Large buyers want a second supplier for bargaining power and delivery certainty, so AMD wins volume commitments once its rack-scale product and software are good enough to run production work.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the Helios racks ship on schedule and whether AMD can get enough packaging and memory allocation to fill the commitments.
entries.statement: AMD converts its Instinct roadmap into material datacenter share.
entries.title: AMD credible second source

entries.falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Cloud operators build their own inference chips to cut the price they pay per unit of work, so each in-house part they deploy is a merchant GPU they do not buy.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house chips can handle training and newer model shapes, not just steady inference work.
entries.statement: Hyperscaler custom silicon meaningfully displaces merchant-GPU demand growth.
entries.title: Custom ASIC substitution

entries.falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
entries.mechanism: Renters bid up whatever is scarce, so prices hold while parts are allocated and soften only where older hardware becomes plentiful.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly the newest racks reach rental fleets, since that is what turns today's scarce part into tomorrow's discounted one.
entries.statement: GPU rental/spot price levels hold up despite added supply.
entries.title: Pricing power persistence

entries.falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Government rules bar the strongest parts from a large buying market, so a share of world demand simply cannot be served no matter how much supply exists.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to policy changes in Washington and Beijing, which can reopen or reclose the market faster than any supply decision.
entries.statement: Export-control policy materially constrains addressable merchant-GPU demand.
entries.title: Export control exposure

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: When the seller lends the money or guarantees the rent, reported orders partly reflect the seller's own credit rather than independent buyer budgets.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the rental income of the financed buyers, because a shortfall there turns guarantees into real costs for the chip vendor.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's own revenue-sharing and credit-support financing increasingly underwrites its accelerator demand, coupling reported demand strength to NVIDIA-extended credit and adding circularity risk to buildout durability.
entries.title: Vendor-financed demand circularity

entries.falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
entries.mechanism: A handful of buyers place most of the orders, so one of them slowing down or switching to its own chips removes a large slice of revenue at once.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly sovereign, enterprise and neocloud buyers grow large enough to dilute the top few accounts.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's data-center revenue is increasingly concentrated in a few direct customers, raising demand-durability risk if any single hyperscaler slows orders or shifts to in-house silicon.
entries.title: Customer concentration risk

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Selling the switches and cabling with the accelerators makes the whole cluster one purchase, which raises the cost of swapping in another vendor's chips.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether open Ethernet fabrics from rival vendors reach the same cluster performance at lower cost.
entries.statement: NVIDIA now leads the data-center Ethernet switch market and sells that networking bundled with its GPUs, deepening a full-system moat that raises switching costs versus standalone accelerators and custom chips. NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching in Q1 2026 by pairing Spectrum-X and Quantum with Blackwell and GB300, and its NVLink systems cut cost per token, but no finding compares networking growth against compute growth, so the sharper claim that networking scales faster than compute is not supported.
entries.title: Networking attach as systems moat

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
entries.mechanism: Each generation lowers the price of serving a unit of model output, which makes uses that were too expensive worth running and lifts total compute bought.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether cheaper serving actually converts into new paid workloads rather than just lower bills on existing ones.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's each-generation drop in cost per token pulls more inference workloads onto its GPUs and widens the market it can serve.
entries.title: Cheaper inference pulls in demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
entries.mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead on non-cancellable memory contracts have already paid for future accelerators, so that demand is committed rather than merely forecast.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the financial health of the depositing buyers, since only a solvent buyer's prepayment is a real lock.
entries.statement: Non-cancelable multi-year HBM contracts backed by billions in customer deposits lock a large share of future accelerator demand into place and reduce the chance that today's buildout is speculative.
entries.title: Prepaid HBM take-or-pay locks in accelerator demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Licences are granted one buyer at a time under a volume cap and a tariff, so the market reopens as a trickle rather than as a return to prior sales.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newest generation is ever cleared, since the licensed parts are a generation behind what buyers want.
entries.statement: China datacenter compute is reopening to NVIDIA only through case-by-case H200- and MI325-class licenses capped under half of comparable US sales, with Chinese buyers now signaling first purchases. This cycle adds H200-class licensing shifted from denial to case-by-case and buyer interest from Alibaba, ByteDance and DeepSeek, broadening the earlier MI325-only picture, while China revenue sits at $4,550M and H200 licenses have booked no revenue yet.
entries.title: Conditional China re-opening with a capped ceiling

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Customers stay with one vendor only while porting their software costs more than the hardware saving, and that porting cost is falling as rival software stacks improve.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to training work rather than inference, since training is where the software gap is still widest.
entries.statement: The difficulty of running existing AI software on non-Nvidia chips keeps customers on Nvidia even when rivals cut hardware prices.
entries.title: CUDA software lock-in sustains the moat

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Memory and flash are a large and rising share of what an AI server costs, so their price increases flow straight into the bill buyers pay per rack.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers pass the cost on or absorb it, which decides whether it hits budgets or system-builder margins.
entries.statement: Fast-rising memory and NVMe prices are pushing up what it costs to build each AI server, which could strain buyer budgets and squeeze system margins.
entries.title: Rising memory costs inflate AI-server economics

entries.falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
entries.mechanism: Several vendors start volume production of new accelerators in the same window, but each ramps at its own pace, so total supply rises in steps spread across a year.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to packaging and memory allocation, because a ramp date means little if the parts to fill it are not available.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's newest racks ramp into production from the third quarter of 2026 while AMD's rack-scale volume mostly arrives in 2027, so the multi-vendor supply wave lands in stages rather than all at once. Supply-chain reporting still has NVIDIA, AMD, AWS and Google parts entering mass production together and AMD's rack reached production with third-quarter shipments, but one account puts AMD's real volume ramp and first production output at the second quarter of 2027 because of manufacturing delays, and Meta's in-house parts only enter production in September.
entries.title: Multi-vendor accelerator supply wave in second-half 2026

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next two quarters.
entries.mechanism: A few named partners account for nearly all of AMD's accelerator commitments, so its growth path rises or falls with those individual decisions.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the gigawatt commitments convert into shipped and paid volume on the stated schedule.
entries.statement: AMD's data-center accelerator growth depends on a small set of very large commitments, which concentrates both its upside and its downside in a handful of partners.
entries.title: AMD growth leans on a few mega-deals

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
entries.mechanism: Using ordinary memory on a simpler package skips the two scarcest steps in accelerator manufacturing, so output is not limited by the same queues.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether ordinary memory bandwidth is enough for the inference work customers actually want to run.
entries.statement: Intel's Crescent Island inference GPU uses standard LPDDR5X memory instead of high-bandwidth memory to sidestep the advanced-packaging and memory bottleneck, opening an alternative supply route for inference chips.
entries.title: Memory-based inference chips route around the packaging bottleneck

entries.falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
entries.mechanism: When many different chip types compete for the same fab and packaging slots, the foundry can fill every line and charge more for each one.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a slowdown in any one large customer segment, which would free capacity and weaken pricing quickly.
entries.statement: AI demand spreading across GPUs, custom ASICs, networking and power chips fills TSMC's capacity across nodes and lets it raise prices.
entries.title: Broadening AI demand tightens TSMC capacity and pricing

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Cloud buyers are spending far ahead of the revenue the new capacity earns, so a disappointing payback would force them to cut orders rather than keep building.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth, which is the visible proof that the spending is earning its keep.
entries.statement: Hyperscalers' sharp jump in AI capital spending risks a pullback if returns disappoint, which would cut accelerator orders.
entries.title: Hyperscaler AI spending may outrun near-term returns

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
entries.mechanism: Customers accept NVIDIA's prices because the alternatives are scarce or slower to deploy, which lets it keep a wide margin even through the costly early phase of a new product.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging input costs, which are rising fast and are the likeliest squeeze on the margin.
entries.statement: NVIDIA keeps its gross margin near three-quarters even while ramping new products, far above rivals, showing buyers still pay premium prices.
entries.title: NVIDIA holds a premium gross margin as it ramps new chips

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
entries.mechanism: A handful of customers book nearly all the advanced-packaging output, so if one steps back there is no queue of other buyers ready to take those slots at the same price.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to custom-chip designers growing their own packaging bookings, which would spread the customer base.
entries.statement: A few AI chip buyers control most of TSMC's advanced-packaging output, so any one of them cutting orders would leave capacity that is hard to refill.
entries.title: AI packaging supply is concentrated in a few buyers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buyers who fear being shut out sign longer contracts to reserve future capacity, which pushes the average delivery date of the order book further out.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how enforceable the long-dated commitments are if a buyer's own demand weakens.
entries.statement: Cloud and chip suppliers are signing longer-dated purchase commitments that push out the average life of their order books, so a growing share of AI compute demand is booked years in advance.
entries.title: Backlog duration lengthens as demand is booked years ahead

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
entries.mechanism: Model providers can only keep buying compute if paying customers keep growing, so their sales figures are the test of whether the buildout rests on real revenue.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to disclosure, since these are private companies and the evidence arrives late and unevenly.
entries.statement: Leading AI model providers are growing revenue fast enough that their heavy compute spending rests on real and rising sales rather than hope.
entries.title: Model-provider revenue scales to underpin the buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next two quarters.
entries.mechanism: With the strongest imported chips barred, Chinese buyers fund domestic suppliers, whose revenue and capability grow because there is no alternative.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic memory and packaging supply, which caps how many domestic accelerators can actually be built.
entries.statement: China's home-grown accelerators can now train frontier-scale models without NVIDIA chips, but Chinese buyers still order far more NVIDIA parts than are available, so the displacement is proven in capability and not yet in volume. Two findings show a 1.6-trillion-parameter model pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators across over 35 trillion tokens, while Chinese firms ordered more than two million restricted NVIDIA parts for 2026 against roughly 700,000 units of inventory and domestic labs' own chips are judged more than two years away.
entries.title: China Domestic Accelerators Displace Banned NVIDIA GPUs

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: These operators buy accelerators years before the rental income arrives, so faster growth means bigger upfront costs and wider losses at the same time.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental price levels, since a drop would push the payback on already-bought fleets further out.
entries.statement: Fast-growing neocloud GPU buyers such as CoreWeave are booking record revenue while their net losses widen.
entries.title: Neocloud GPU Buyers Grow Revenue but Deepen Losses

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
entries.mechanism: An accelerator only earns money once it is plugged into a powered building, so available electricity and grid equipment set the real deployment ceiling.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to gains in work done per megawatt, which stretch a fixed power budget across more compute.
entries.statement: Companies now size and cap their AI buildouts by gigawatts of available power, so electricity and site capacity increasingly limit how many accelerators they can actually deploy.
entries.title: Power capacity is becoming the binding limit on AI buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
entries.mechanism: Cloud firms design the chip idea but hand the hard engineering to outside partners, so the escape route from merchant GPUs runs through the same two firms.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a third design partner or an in-house team lands a large production programme.
entries.statement: Hyperscalers' shift to custom AI chips runs almost entirely through two outside design firms, so the alternative to merchant GPUs is itself concentrated in those two suppliers.
entries.title: The custom-AI-chip alternative depends on two design houses

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for two consecutive months.
entries.mechanism: Contract manufacturers bill only when finished servers leave the factory, so their monthly sales are a direct read on machines actually shipping.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages, since a memory or packaging gap stops the line regardless of order intake.
entries.statement: Contract server makers post record monthly revenue as AI-server and networking orders ship in volume.
entries.title: ODM AI-server revenue confirms real shipments

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Accelerator fleets are bought with borrowed money against future rental contracts, so the equity cushion stays thin while the debt grows with each purchase.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and to how long rented hardware keeps its earning power.
entries.statement: Neocloud operators fund their GPU fleets mostly with debt, leaving thin equity cushions.
entries.title: Neocloud GPU buyers carry heavy debt loads

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Putting the optics inside the switch package moves cluster wiring onto the semiconductor supply chain, so networking capacity now depends on packaging lines rather than pluggable module vendors.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to packaging capacity, because the same lines are already stretched by accelerator demand.
entries.statement: The move to co-packaged optics is reshaping how AI networking gear is built and supplied, tying cluster wiring to a fast-changing optics roadmap.
entries.title: Optical networking shifts to co-packaged optics as a supply lever

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
entries.mechanism: Building fabrication, packaging and assembly inside the United States adds capacity that does not depend on a single island, which widens the supply base over time.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and equipment timelines, since announced dollars only matter once a line is running.
entries.statement: NVIDIA and its partners are committing to build AI hardware inside the United States at very large scale, adding fabrication and packaging capacity outside Taiwan.
entries.title: US onshoring broadens the AI hardware supply base

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Providers cannot deliver contracts faster than they can build capacity, so signed commitments show demand earlier and more fully than reported sales do.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the backlog is cancellable, since soft commitments would overstate real demand.
entries.statement: Cloud providers are booking compute contracts far faster than they can deliver them, so their reported backlogs now show demand better than their quarterly sales do.
entries.title: Cloud backlog conversion becomes the demand proof point

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Building capacity now costs more than these businesses generate in cash, so the gap is filled with borrowed money and new shares.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions, because dearer borrowing would force spending discipline quickly.
entries.statement: The largest cloud buyers are turning to debt and share issuance to pay for AI capacity instead of funding it from cash generated by their businesses.
entries.title: Hyperscalers now borrow to fund the buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
entries.mechanism: Each generation does more work for the same electricity, so a buyer with a fixed power budget can keep adding capability without adding megawatts.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to vendor claims versus measured results, since much of the evidence comes from the sellers.
entries.statement: Each new generation of AI racks does far more work per megawatt, which lets buyers add capacity even when power and packaging are capped.
entries.title: Efficiency gains stretch scarce power and packaging

entries.falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for two consecutive quarters before end-2027.
entries.mechanism: Every accelerator needs a fixed number of memory stacks, so once memory output is fully sold the number of accelerators that can be finished is fixed too.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fab output arriving, since stacked memory uses about three times the wafer capacity of standard memory.
entries.statement: Stacked memory, not chips or packaging alone, now decides how many accelerators NVIDIA and AMD can actually deliver.
entries.title: Memory supply is the new choke point on accelerator shipments

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier gross margin falls for two consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
entries.mechanism: Memory suppliers are the scarce link in the chain, so they set prices and keep more of the value in each AI server for themselves.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity, which historically turns extraordinary margins into ordinary ones fast.
entries.statement: Memory suppliers are earning extraordinary margins on AI parts, shifting profit from the server builders toward the memory makers.
entries.title: Memory makers capture a growing share of AI server profit

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Governments and large firms are buying whole clusters of their own rather than renting, which adds a buyer group that sits outside the big cloud operators.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to public budgets and political commitment, which move on slower and less predictable cycles than cloud spending.
entries.statement: National projects and large enterprises are now placing accelerator orders big enough to matter alongside the cloud giants.
entries.title: Sovereign and enterprise buyers become a new demand tier

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Intel is winning back server processor sales and outside manufacturing work at improving margins, which puts a third supplier back into the AI hardware chain.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its newest process reaches volume yields, since the foundry recovery rests on that.
entries.statement: Intel's data-center and foundry businesses are growing again with better margins, adding a third source of AI-adjacent supply.
entries.title: Intel returns as a data-center supplier

entries.falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Chip vendors put their own money into the firms that buy their chips, so part of reported demand is funded by the seller rather than by outside investors.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the funded customers raise independent capital, which would show the demand stands on its own.
entries.statement: Merchant accelerator vendors are now buying equity stakes in the AI firms that buy their chips, tying reported demand to vendor-funded customers beyond NVIDIA alone.
entries.title: chipmakers take equity in their own customers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for two consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
entries.mechanism: Memory makers shift their lines to the highest-priced AI parts, which starves ordinary memory buyers and lifts prices on everyday products.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new fabrication capacity comes online, since none is expected before late 2026.
entries.statement: The stacked-memory shortage is spreading into standard memory and raising prices on consumer and general-purpose graphics parts.
entries.title: memory crunch spills into consumer and general-purpose parts

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for two consecutive quarters through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Accelerator makers contract directly with memory suppliers because reserved memory output is what determines how many chips they can finish.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these reservations displace other buyers or simply reprice the same limited output.
entries.statement: Accelerator makers are signing multi-year partnerships and joint development deals straight with memory suppliers to reserve future stacked-memory output.
entries.title: Chip vendors buy their memory supply directly

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within four quarters as rivals ship volume.
entries.mechanism: One supplier makes most of the stacked memory and the biggest buyers have booked its output, so whoever holds a contract with that supplier can build AI servers and others cannot.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether rival suppliers qualify their next-generation stacks at the same yields and dates.
entries.statement: One supplier holds most of the stacked-memory market and the largest cloud buyers have locked up long-term contracts, so access to that single source now decides who can build AI servers.
entries.title: Stacked-memory supply sits with one dominant maker

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists raise the personal and commercial cost of reselling restricted chips, which shuts the informal channels that used to carry them.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to enforcement outside Taiwan, since routes can shift to jurisdictions with less scrutiny.
entries.statement: Criminal investigations and tighter buyer whitelists are shutting the informal channels that moved restricted AI chips into China.
entries.title: Enforcement closes the gray route into China

entries.falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
entries.mechanism: Packaging capacity can be added by building more lines and hiring outside assembly partners, while memory needs new fabs and long production cycles, so packaging loosens first.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much packaging each new accelerator generation consumes, since bigger parts can absorb the added capacity.
entries.statement: Advanced-packaging capacity is expanding fast enough to narrow the shortfall from about 20% to about 10% by the end of 2026, but lead times stay at 52 to 78 weeks with bookings into 2027 and TSMC says the demand gap runs through 2029-2030, so packaging eases only slowly while memory stays the tighter of the two limits. Capacity is rising toward 125,000 to 130,000 wafers a month, could approach 200,000 including outside assembly partners, and outside packaging houses are adding capacity while NVIDIA weighs moving some output to Intel's packaging, yet memory shows no easing at all with suppliers warning of tightness through 2027 and into 2028.
entries.title: Packaging tightness starts to ease while memory does not

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for two consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
entries.mechanism: The newest racks hold far more flash storage per system, so each one shipped consumes a large block of an industry that was not sized for it.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast the newest generation actually deploys, since the demand step only lands with those racks.
entries.statement: The newest accelerator generation adds a large storage tier that is pulling flash demand up sharply and is already showing up as rising server costs.
entries.title: Storage becomes the next scarce part in the AI rack

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Public list rates for the newest rack-scale systems appear on major provider pricing pages within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: When the newest systems are scarce, providers sell them through negotiation instead of a list price so they can charge what each buyer will pay.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply of the newest racks, since published prices tend to return once a part is no longer allocated.
entries.statement: Cloud providers publish rates for last-generation accelerators but quote their newest systems only through sales, so listed prices no longer show what the leading edge costs.
entries.title: The newest systems leave the public price list

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
entries.mechanism: The total market is growing faster than NVIDIA can supply, so rivals absorb the overflow and gain share while NVIDIA's own sales keep rising.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether NVIDIA's supply constraints ease, because a vendor that can ship everything buyers want stops leaking share.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's share of AI accelerators is falling even as its revenue sets records, so rivals are taking growth rather than taking business away.
entries.title: NVIDIA's share slips while its sales still grow

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Selling a finished rack bundles chips, networking, cooling and software into one decision, which shifts competition from chip specifications to whole-system output per dollar and per megawatt.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards, which would let buyers mix vendors again and undo the bundling.
entries.statement: Both merchant vendors now sell whole 72-accelerator racks with their own networking and software rather than individual chips, so buyers compare complete systems instead of parts.
entries.title: The rack, not the chip, is now the unit of competition

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Power transformer lead times fall below 80 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: A site cannot energise without transformers and switchgear that take two to four years to arrive, so ordering that equipment sets the earliest date accelerators can be plugged in.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to transformer factory expansion, which is slow and serves many industries beyond data centers.
entries.statement: Power transformers and similar grid equipment now take years to deliver, so new AI sites are held up by electrical gear rather than by chips.
entries.title: Grid equipment lead times gate new AI sites

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
entries.mechanism: Buyers pay up for whatever is scarce and fast, so as older hardware becomes plentiful its rate falls while the newest systems command a rising premium.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast the newest racks reach rental fleets, which is what eventually turns today's premium part into a discounted one.
entries.statement: Rental prices for the newest systems are rising while quotes for the previous generation spread out and drift lower, so the price premium is concentrating in whatever just launched.
entries.title: The rental premium moves to the newest hardware
